author: Shibasis Rath
headline: AutoDNA Autonomous Lab Runs DNA Synthesis From a Prompt
text: An AI multi-agent system at Shanghai Jiao Tong University orchestrated more than 20 instruments to perform nucleic-acid synthesis, storage and mutation detection. Only reagent top-ups from people were needed. In one demonstration, the system took a plain-English request. It encoded a digital message into 78 DNA strands, synthesized them, stored the molecules, sequenced them back and recovered the original content exactly. The same platform achieved a measured enzymatic DNA synthesis yield of 97.8%, matching published expert-optimized results. Researchers from Shanghai Jiao Tong University describe the system, called AutoDNA, in Nature. Reference: Wu M, Wang Z, Wang J, et al. An AI-native experimental laboratory for autonomous biomolecular operations. Nature (2026). DOI: 10.1038/s41586-026-11228-6 (peer-reviewed).
